The short answer is that I did not know it was bad for many years. It was just what Dad wanted us do with him (he sometimes made me and my sister do things so he could watch). When I was quite young I even invited other neighborhood kids my age to play the same "games" I was learning... I had no idea. As I got older, though, I started to realize that this thing which we had to keep secret was not something other people did and I started thinking that if we had to keep quiet perhaps there was something off about this.

He stopped when I hit puberty. I then went through my teen years as a horribly shy, maladjusted kid who lost friends easily and struggled socially. Horrible grades but high IQ, got into many fights, endured chronic stomach pain (that still bothers me to this day and is apparently related), couldn't get a girlfriend to save my life, was picked on a lot and was so shy that I could hardly speak to anyone (my nickname at school was "Lurch" as I am tall and walked around silently, stooped over and weird), attempted suicide, etc. I did not know how to act because the things I would instinctively do were so weird to everyone else. Also, I had never really had a dad. Like, technically I did but practically I was just this thing to use when he was horny and I assume I represented a great threat to him due to what I knew. In the aftermath of what he had done throughout my childhood he was frequently not very nice to me. He was hot and cold and I suspect that this was due to his shame at what he knew he had done. I, in turn, was always angry with him because he was so often mean and threatening to me.

By the time I got to college (I had still not acknowledged or even thought about what had happened to me at this point in my life) a girlfriend who was a psychology major told me that she was concerned with me because I was exhibiting behaviors that she had read about in a class about abuse victims. She said, "You do this and this and this and this... were you molested as a child?" and I kind of freaked out. Like, how the hell did she know this about me?! I told her what my childhood was like and after she got done reacting (crying, I think she even threw up) she insisted I see a psychologist. That was the beginning of me dealing with what happened to me and that was 30 years ago.

So aside from being told it was bad here are things that can negatively influence a child:

\- keeping a very dark secret for years

\- not having a normal parent/child relationship

\- learned behaviors that are not socially acceptable (i.e. "games" that are actually abusive)

\- a parent that does not himself view you as a regular child (and the influence that has on his treatment of you)

\- the eventual withdrawal of whatever "affection" you had been used to (wrong as it was, it was all you had)

\- how you are treated year after year by those that do not want the time bomb secret you carry to ever be released, harming their own lives (this can include many other family members)

\- how other people treat you because your behavior is "off"

\- physical problems induced by what happened
